executive_summary: A live GEO audit of TransGlobal Holding Company found a technically accessible site with a GEO score of 58/100. The numeric score comes from the geo-seo-claude audit model, while the advisory recommendations come from a separate ReScience optimization pass. The most urgent content issue is low citability at 28.0/100. The most urgent structural issue is the missing llms.txt guidance layer. The homepage also needs cleaner information architecture because it currently exposes 10 H1 tags. ReScience optimization pass focuses on actionable SEO/GEO execution rather than a second weighted score. The biggest structural gap is the missing llms.txt guidance layer. The biggest content gap is weak answer-first formatting and low factual density.

findings.title: Key pages are not AI-citation ready
findings.summary: Average citability scored 28.0/100, which means priority pages are still weak candidates for extraction into AI-generated answers.
findings.description: Average citability scored 28.0/100, which means priority pages are still weak candidates for extraction into AI-generated answers.
findings.leadership_impact: Low citation readiness reduces the brand's chance of appearing in AI answers during high-intent discovery, which directly limits awareness, assisted conversion, and competitive share of voice.
findings.marketing_action: Rewrite service, solution, and explainer pages into answer-first sections with sourced statistics, clear proof points, and short extractable paragraphs.
findings.developer_action: Support content templates with one clear H1, stronger H2/H3 structure, and reusable placements for FAQ and supporting schema on high-priority pages.
findings.observed_evidence: The live audit measured average citability at 28.0/100, below the threshold where pages are typically easy for AI systems to quote and attribute.

findings.title: llms.txt guidance files are missing
findings.summary: The site does not expose llms.txt guidance files at the root, so AI systems receive no direct guidance about priority pages, document structure, or recommended crawl targets.
findings.description: The site does not expose llms.txt guidance files at the root, so AI systems receive no direct guidance about priority pages, document structure, or recommended crawl targets.
findings.leadership_impact: Without a machine-readable guidance layer, the company has less control over how AI systems discover and prioritize its most valuable content.
findings.marketing_action: Publish llms.txt and llms-full.txt that point AI systems to the pages most aligned with brand messaging, core services, and thought-leadership assets.
findings.developer_action: Create and deploy root-level llms.txt files, keep them versioned with the site, and update them whenever priority URLs or content architecture changes.
findings.observed_evidence: The live fetch did not find llms.txt at the expected root path, so no AI guidance document is currently published.

findings.title: Heading architecture is diluted
findings.summary: The homepage currently exposes 10 H1 tags instead of one clear primary page thesis, which weakens how both users and AI systems interpret topical focus.
findings.description: The homepage currently exposes 10 H1 tags instead of one clear primary page thesis, which weakens how both users and AI systems interpret topical focus.
findings.leadership_impact: A diluted page thesis makes the brand's most important landing page less clear, which can suppress message retention and reduce AI confidence in the page's core topic.
findings.marketing_action: Clarify the homepage message hierarchy so the primary value proposition is unmistakable, then align supporting sections to secondary audience and service themes.
findings.developer_action: Refactor heading markup to a single H1 with semantically ordered H2 and H3 sections, and remove layout-driven heading misuse.
findings.observed_evidence: The homepage audit found 10 H1 tags, a strong sign that content hierarchy is being split across multiple competing signals.

findings.title: Optimization opportunities remain after the base audit
findings.summary: ReScience optimization pass focuses on actionable SEO/GEO execution rather than a second weighted score. The biggest structural gap is the missing llms.txt guidance layer. The biggest content gap is weak answer-first formatting and low factual density.
findings.description: ReScience optimization pass focuses on actionable SEO/GEO execution rather than a second weighted score. The biggest structural gap is the missing llms.txt guidance layer. The biggest content gap is weak answer-first formatting and low factual density.
findings.leadership_impact: The site has a workable foundation, but unresolved optimization gaps will keep the brand from reaching stronger AI visibility gains without a coordinated follow-through plan.
findings.marketing_action: Turn the ReScience recommendations into an execution backlog for content refreshes, proof-point additions, and platform-specific improvements.
findings.developer_action: Bundle the structural recommendations into roadmap work so schema, content modules, and technical trust signals are implemented consistently.
findings.observed_evidence: The advisory pass still flagged medium-priority optimization work, which indicates the site can improve even after the baseline audit score is calculated.

findings.title: Entity trust signals are still thin
findings.summary: Brand identity appears across social platforms, but stronger authoritative entity reinforcement is still missing.
findings.description: Brand identity appears across social platforms, but stronger authoritative entity reinforcement is still missing.
findings.leadership_impact: Thin entity trust makes it harder for AI systems to confidently associate the brand with its services, expertise, and authority.
findings.marketing_action: Strengthen third-party validation through consistent profile governance, citation-worthy proof points, and broader entity reinforcement across trusted platforms.
findings.developer_action: Align visible profile links, organization schema, and sameAs references so the site publishes one consistent entity graph.
findings.observed_evidence: The audit found social presence but did not confirm stronger authority anchors such as Wikipedia or Wikidata-level entity reinforcement.
